transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-11-05
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Laura Bennett, Chloe Martin, Ethan Park, Samir Desai, Priya Shah, Jordan Lee

Summary (auto)
- Customer asked about recent 'model switching' behavior during an EU incident and how pinning is enforced.
- Redwood reviewed mitigation and upcoming guardrails for unintended fallback.
- Discussed reliability expectations and status communication.

Transcript
[00:00] Laura Bennett: Cool, thanks everyone for joining. This is our QBR plus a follow-up on the EU thing from last month.
[00:18] Samir Desai: Yeah, the big question for us is the, um, it looked like failover? Like the model changed under us even though we pin the model.
[00:32] Ethan Park: Right. In that window in eu-west, the router was incorrectly selecting the fallback variant. It should not have happened while primary capacity was healthy.
[00:49] Priya Shah: We saw it in the header. It said a different model string. Also outputs were more, like, verbose and sometimes refused.
[01:05] Chloe Martin: Support saw the same across a few accounts. We tied it to an incident and rolled back within about two hours.
[01:18] Jordan Lee: Is that the same thing as your normal degradation behavior? Like if the GPUs are full you move traffic?
[01:28] Ethan Park: Normally, yes, we have a fallback policy for capacity loss. This was unintended because a policy tweak made the router think it was overloaded based on a noisy signal.
[01:51] Samir Desai: So pinning is not absolute?
[01:55] Ethan Park: Pinning is intended to be preserved; the fallback logic ran earlier than the pin-preference rule. We added a guardrail: strict pin + healthy primary means no fallback evaluation.
[02:17] Priya Shah: We need to be sure it doesn't happen again. Our evals were failing and we had to pause a rollout.
[02:27] Laura Bennett: Totally understood. We'll share the incident write-up and we're adding canaries specifically to detect 'pinned model not honored' before any policy rollout.
[03:01] Samir Desai: OK. Also in the future can we get faster comms? We saw it before the status page.
[03:08] Chloe Martin: That's fair. We are tuning alerts so we declare faster when fallback selection rate spikes without capacity loss.
[03:35] Jordan Lee: Just to benchmark, OpenAI never shows model switching but we know it's behind the scenes. Bedrock was worse for us.
[03:47] Laura Bennett: Makes sense. For us, we surface the model id to be transparent, but that also means you can see when something is off.
[04:10] Ethan Park: If you can send us a small set of pinned prompts that are sensitive, we can include them in our invariant test suite for eu-west.
[04:24] Priya Shah: Yep, we can do that.
[45:10] Laura Bennett: Recap: we send the postmortem link, you send prompts, and we'll confirm the header behavior for hosted vs dedicated. Thanks everyone.
